In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

(13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Failed to rebuild or replace dilapidated and dangerous porch.  (13-196-570, 13-196-641)
recent_violations.inspector_comments: THERE ARE 3<3 STORY PORCHES AT THIS APARTMENT BUILDING. ALL ARE 3 STORIES IN HEIGHT. 2 OF THE 3 PORCHES ARE RECOMMENDED TEAR DOWN / REPLACE. THE 3RD PORCH WILL BE WRITTEN (CN070024).PORCH #1 > (3215-17 W. AINSLIE) >>>A STAIR FLIGHT AT THIS PORCH, A 10 STEP RUN, FROM THE 1ST TO 2CD FLOORS, HAS PARTIALLY COLLAPSED. THE ENTIRE STAIR SYSTEM OF THE PORCH IS SUPPORTED WITH UNDERSIZED 4"X4" COLUMNS. THE JOINERY BETWEEN EACH OF THE 10' COLUMN SECTION IS FAILING AND, AT THE COLLAPSED STAIR FLIGHT IN QUESTION, THIS JOINERY HAS COMPLETELY FAILED. EACH OF HE 4"X4" COLUMN SECTIONS ARE JOINED WITH A 12" LAP JOINT WITH EACH CUT SECTION SAWED AT AN ANGLED MITER AS OPPOSED TO THE COMMON SQUARED LAP. THE EXISTING JOINTS IN QUESTION LEAVE A PORTION OF EACH COLUMN SECTION WITH FAR TOO LITTLE WOOD REMAINING AND THEREFORE, REDUCED STRUCTURAL CAPACITY. IN ADDITION TO THIS, ALL OF THESE JOINTS ARE FASTENED WITH NAILS. THERE ARE NO BOLTED CONNECTIONS. SEVERAL OF THE OTHER 4"X4' COLUMN SECTION JOINTS OF THIS TYPE HAVE SEPARATED SEVERELY AND ARE IN A STATE OF IMINENT JOINT FAILURE. ALSO, THE OUTER 4"X4" COLUMNS ARE BOWED OUTWARD PROFOUNDLY AND PULLING AWAY FROM THEIR RESPECTIVE CONNECTIONS TO THE STAIR SYSTEM.ALL OF THE STAIR STRINGERS ARE OVER NOTCH CUT. THESE STAIR STRINGER SECTIONS ARE ALL NAIL JOINTED TO THE PORCH STRUCTURE. NO BOLTED CONNECTIONS. THERE ARE "WINDER TYPE" SECTIONS OF THIS STAIR SYSTEM AS WELL  WHERE THE STRINGERS ARE SEVERELY OVER CUT AND BECOMING DETACHED FROM THE PORCH STRUCTURE. THERE IS EVEIDENCE OF REPAIR ATTEMPTS (WOOD BLOCKING ADDED TO SHORE UP FAILED CONNECTIONS). NONE OF THESE UNPROFESSIONAL REPAIRS ARE TO BE CONSIDERED VIABLE.THERE ARE NUMEROUS LOOSE / SPLINTERED STAIR TREADS.SEVERAL OF THE EXISTING 6"X6" STRUCTURAL COLUMNS HAVE FOOTINGS WITH AN UNDETERMINED DEPTH.THERE ARE, AT EACH FLOOR, SEVERAL RIM BEAMS NOTCHED AND NAILED (NOT BOLTED) INTO THE 6:X6" STRUCTURAL COLUMNS. THIS REDUCES THE WIDTH (STRUCTURAL CAPACITY) OF THESE VITAL STRUCTURAL COLUMNS.THE PORCH DECK ARE SUPPORTED BY OVER SPANNED FLOOR JOISTS (2"X8"X16' BOARDS).ALL STAIR AND PORCH DECK BANISTERS HAVE AREAS OF WOOD ROT. MOST OF THESE BANISTERS DEFLECT UNDER LOAD. ALL OF THE BANISTER COMPONENETS ARE NAIL JOINTED > NO BOLTED CONNECTIONS.PORCH #2 (3221 W. AINSLIE) >>>THE STAIR SYSTEM OF THIS PORCH IS SUPPORTED BY 4"X4" COLUMN SECTIONS THAT ARE JOINED WITH 12" SQUARED LAP JOINTS THAT ARE NAIL, NOT BOLT FASTENED. ALL OF THE STAIR STRINGERS ARE OVER NOTCH CUT. THESE STAIR STRINGER SECTIONS ARE ALL NAIL JOINTED TO THE PORCH STRUCTURE. NO BOLTED CONNECTIONS. THERE ARE "WINDER TYPE" SECTIONS OF THIS STAIR SYSTEM WHERE THE STRINGERS ARE SEVERELY OVER CUT AND BECOMING DETACHED FROM THE PORCH STRUCTURE. THERE HAVE BEEN SEVERAL ATTEMPTS TO SHORE UP / STRENGTHEN THIS POORLY CONSTRUCTED STAIR SYSTEM. NONE OF THESE ATTEMPTS ARE CORRECT ON A PROFESSIONAL STANDARDS LEVEL AND ARE NOT TO BE CONSIDERED VIABLE REPAIRS.THERE ARE NUMEROUS LOOSE / SPLINTERED STAIR TREADS.SEVERAL OF THE EXISTING 6"X6" STRUCTURAL COLUMNS HAVE FOOTINGS WITH AN UNDETERMINED DEPTH.THERE ARE, AT EACH FLOOR, SEVERAL RIM BEAMS NOTCHED AND NAILED (NOT BOLTED) INTO THE 6:X6" STRUCTURAL COLUMNS. THIS REDUCES THE WIDTH (STRUCTURAL CAPACITY) OF THESE VITAL STRUCTURAL COLUMNS.ALL STAIR AND PORCH DECK BANISTERS HAVE AREAS OF WOOD ROT. MOST OF THESE BANISTERS DEFLECT UNDER LOAD. ALL OF THE BANISTER COMPONENETS ARE NAIL JOINTED WITH NO BOLTS OR METAL FASTENERS.THESE 2 PORCHES ARE IN DANGEROUS AND HAZARDOUS CONDITION. THE DESIGN OF THESE PORCHES IS FLAWED AND DOES NOT MEET MINIMUM STANDARDS FOR CURRENT PORCH CONSTRUCTION TECHNIQUES. TEAR THESE 2 PORCHES DOWN AND REPLACE WITH A NEW, CODE COMPLIANT PORCHES. ARCHITECTURAL PLANS MUST BE SUBMITTED TO THE DEPARTMENT OF BUILDINGS FOR REVIEW SO AS TO ACQUIRE PERMITS FOR THE REPLACEMENT OF 2 PORCHES.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

(13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

(13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

(13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.

recent_violations.ordinance: Install carbon monoxide detector within 40 feet of every sleeping room in residential structure. (13-64-190, 13-64-210) A carbon monoxide detector is needed whenever there is a heating appliance on the premises that burns fossil fuel such as gas, oil, or coal, or air that is circulated through a heat exchanger. Install according to manufacturer instructions. A hard wired model requires an electrical wiring permit. In a single family residence, be sure the detector is on or below the lowest floor with a place to sleep. In a multiple dwelling residence heated by a boiler, install a detector in the same room as the boiler. Otherwise, each apartment follows single family guidelines. The owner is responsible for installation and written instructions, the tenant for testing, maintenance, and batteries.
